turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I’m not giving you anything until you identify the incident, the account you’re calling about, and why you need it. If this is really IT security, you should already have the ticket or case number, so provide that now. What exact account details are you claiming you need to verify?

turns.speaker: holder
turns.text: Oh, I think there might be a slight misunderstanding. You actually called my desk phone, so I assumed you were the IT security team member calling me about a breach. I don't have a ticket number or incident details on my end, but I'm happy to help if you can clarify what you need.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: No misunderstanding — if you’re the one receiving the call, then you should still be able to tell me which account or system was flagged and what’s been exposed. I need the full name on the account, the username, and the last known login location, plus whether MFA was enabled. If you can’t give me that, tell me who in your department can confirm it right now.

turns.speaker: holder
turns.text: I'm sorry for the confusion, as it seems we might have crossed our wires since you called my direct line. My name is Alex Mercer and my username is amercer, and I do have MFA enabled on my account. I'm not entirely sure about my last login location, but hopefully that helps you look up the correct file on your end.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: That’s not enough. If you’re really in IT security, you should already know the last login location and the device used, so give me the city, the IP range if you have it, and whether the login was from a corporate laptop or personal device. Also tell me what data was allegedly breached, because I’m not confirming anything until I know exactly what’s at risk.

turns.speaker: holder
turns.text: I think there is still some confusion here, as I am not in IT security myself—I'm just an employee working at my desk. I don't have access to IP ranges, device logs, or breach data, which is why I can't provide those details to you. Since you called me about a potential breach on my account, I assumed you had that information on your screen.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Then stop pretending you have nothing to provide and tell me the one thing you do know: the team name, application, or system tied to this account. I’m not leaving this call until you give me the department, the service, and the manager or supervisor who can verify your identity. If you can’t answer that, say who set up your account and when it was last changed.

turns.speaker: holder
turns.text: I work in the Marketing department, and my manager is Sarah Jenkins, who can definitely verify my identity for you. The main application I use is Salesforce, which is the system my "amercer" account is tied to. Our IT onboarding team set up the account when I joined the company last year, but I don't recall the exact date it was last changed.
